assessment: Do not substitute v0.1.17 into the v0.33 candidate as a kernel-only upgrade. A separate coordinated Torch/SYCL-TLA/build-layout migration is feasible in principle but is not yet validated or justified by demonstrated performance on the deployed dense Qwen profile.

blockers_for_unchanged_packaging.requirement: Coherent Torch ABI and upstream dependency selection
blockers_for_unchanged_packaging.evidence: vLLM v0.33 requirements/xpu.txt pins torch==2.14.0 and vllm_xpu_kernels==0.1.15.4. Kernel v0.1.17 pyproject.toml and requirements.txt pin torch==2.15.0+xpu, and CMakeLists.txt expects 2.15.0. Official release notes explicitly require the matching Torch environment.
blockers_for_unchanged_packaging.effect: Current Nix Torch2.14/Triton3.8/torchvision0.29 closure cannot be treated as the supported v0.1.17 environment. CMake merely warns on an unexpected Torch version; this is not compatibility evidence. Existing native binaries cannot establish compatibility with rebuilt Torch2.15 binaries.
blockers_for_unchanged_packaging.minimum_action: Resolve exact compatible Torch2.15 XPU, Triton, torchvision and runtime/toolchain dependencies; rebuild all native extensions and consumers; explicitly reconcile vLLM's exact Torch2.14 pin and qualify that exception instead of deleting dependency checks.

Nix mk-kernels.nix still builds grouped_gemm_xe_default, makes grouped_gemm_xe_2 depend on it, and composes/exports the old library.

interface_review.change: Native schema changes from logits, num_sampled_tokens, max_num_kept, max_compact_support to logits, cu_num_logits, num_sampled_tokens, max_num_kept, max_compact_support, rows_per_request.
interface_review.assessment: Breaking for direct old native callers, but not a demonstrated serving break here: git grep of both frozen v0.33 and old fork finds only the local Triton _compact_sampling_mask_kernel in vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/output.py, not a torch.ops._xpu_C.compact_sampling_mask call. Do not count this schema difference alone as a blocker for the current profile.

Existing upstream gdn_attention and ordinary spec/non-spec schemas remain compatible with v0.33 _gdn_attention_core_xpu_impl. The downstream split_mixed_non_spec trailing argument is still absent upstream and must be replayed with its paired vLLM caller. New native RecoverSSM entrypoint has no Qwen GDN caller in frozen v0.33: its _xpu_ops.py continues to dispatch gdn_attention and its ReplaySSM config validates supported architectures. Kernel availability alone does not enable Qwen recurrent-memory savings.
interface_review.new_runtime_risks: v0.1.17 changes causal-convolution null-state handling from <=-1 to <=0, adds 64-bit convolution-state offsets and DeepSeek layout support. Review all seven downstream patches against these changes and run native mixed/spec/padded and cache-lifecycle tests; do not infer the old tiled-path corruption or fresh-state barrier requirement is fixed from unrelated layout changes.

interface_review.assessment: Public Python flash_attn_varlen_func and native varlen_fwd call shapes used by v0.33 remain available. v0.1.17 changes speculative fast-path row mapping to handle ragged and padded queries and places it under fallback handling. This is a plausible benefit for adaptive verification or BF16 paged draft attention, but the KVarN target path and ordinary eager profile need dispatch tracing before any throughput claim.

XpuFusedMoe keeps the v0.33 keyword constructor/apply arguments and adds optional quantization/activation hooks; it also changes device-dependent weight layouts and mutates parameters once. Existing v0.33 xpu_moe.py uses keyword arguments. Added optional defaults for MLA skip_scale, multimodal mrope_interleaved and quantization expert_scale_desc preserve old argument calls. This is static signature compatibility only; MoE numerical and loading tests remain required for the generic package. The deployed 27B dense model does not use the new Qwen3.6-35B-A3B fused MoE path.

source_projection_review.base_glue: Existing projection retains all non-FlashAttention csrc files, including new csrc/sycl_launch.h used by csrc/cache.cpp and new ngram source, so no missing base-header issue was found.
source_projection_review.fa2_glue: Its include closure remains csrc/utils.h, core/ and public attention headers when Xe3P is disabled. No new omitted header was found in this bounded review.
source_projection_review.split_libraries: Whole selected subtrees remain included, but the deleted grouped_gemm_xe_default build target requires the migration above.
source_projection_review.architecture: Keep the B70 override aotDevices=[bmg] and both Nix split/glue Xe3P OFF settings. v0.1.17 defaults Xe3P ON and folds CRI targets into AOT when enabled. Enabling Xe3P would expand build scope without a B70 benefit.

intermediate_v0164.assessment: Not a Torch2.14-compatible escape hatch. It also pins Torch2.15; its tip 4e38707669b8f44a47afcdc68b7d5dc223de66c0 is the Torch dependency bump.
intermediate_v0164.smaller_build_delta: Retains SYCL-TLA 87f6850 and XE_DEFAULT layout. All four existing packaging patches individually pass zero-fuzz dry runs against the exact tag source.
intermediate_v0164.missing_v017_opportunities: Does not contain the ragged adaptive-verification FlashAttention fast-path update or token-aware fused QK/RoPE change. Its principal attention optimization is head_size=72 MoonViT; no direct dense W4A16 matmul implementation change was found.
intermediate_v0164.recommendation: Do not adopt it solely as a compromise version: it still expands the Torch upgrade scope, without demonstrated B70/Qwen gains. A different intermediate release would require its own exact tag/dependency/performance audit.
